turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Good morning sir. Kindly sit, I will check the pressure and temperature before doctor sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Actually I am a bit tensed only.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Keep the arm loose. Blood pressure is one thirty over eighty four, and the pulse is ninety six.
[SEG0004] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Temperature is thirty seven point eight, oxygen saturation ninety eight percent, and respirations about eighteen per minute.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Last night at home the thermometer showed a hundred and one point two. My wife checked it.
[SEG0006] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I will mention that to doctor. This dressing is from the hernia operation, is it?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, right side groin. They operated ten days back.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, I am Dr. Shah. I have those numbers. Tell me what is troubling you.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, the wound is red and some dirty fluid is coming. When it started I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Redness and discharge, and the start date is not clear to you.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Maybe two days, maybe three. I cannot say properly.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did you have fever?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Last night only I was feeling hot. This morning it is gone, I am not feeling feverish now.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any shivering with that fever?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No shivering.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is the wound paining?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes it is paining, more than last week, but not severe.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does the pain get worse when you walk?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will not record that as a definite feature. Is the fluid foul smelling?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes, not really. I cannot say for sure.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting, loose motions, or burning when you pass urine?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain or breathlessness?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No doctor.

[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me say it back. Ten days after a right groin hernia operation, the wound is red with dirty discharge, you cannot date the onset, there was fever last night which has settled, the pain is present but not severe, and there is no vomiting, loose motion, burning urine, chest pain or breathlessness.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, correct. One more thing, I was putting coconut oil on it, neighbour told me. I stopped that yesterday.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Kindly do not put oil, turmeric, or any paste. We will repeat that advice at the end.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Which tablets did the hospital send?

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Augmentin, the big one, six hundred twenty five maybe, three times a day. I don't know if the dose is exact, and some afternoons I forgot, so I am not sure I took it properly.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): How many days was that course?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Five days... or was it seven? I finished the strip. It is not with me now.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Finished, then. Dose uncertain, some doses missed, length five or seven. I will not make it neater than that.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Brufen also, four hundred milligram morning and night for the pain. I stopped it two days back because of acidity.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ibuprofen four hundred milligrams twice a day, stopped two days ago. What about pain relief now?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Crocin five hundred milligram, by mouth, two times a day when it pains.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Paracetamol five hundred, twice daily, ongoing. Was there a constipation syrup?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Lactulose, they gave it, but I never took it. Not even once. It is sitting in the fridge.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then it is not a medicine you are on. Any drug allergy, penicillin or otherwise?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No allergy at all.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Diabetes or blood pressure before this?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing ongoing. I don't smoke. I am staying with my wife and son. I work in a bank, on leave now.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fine. I need the dressing removed. Could you take it off?
[SEG0044] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Yes doctor. Sir, relaxing the leg, I am peeling it now. It is a little stuck.
[SEG0045] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): The gauze has yellow stain, a moderate amount, not soaked through the whole pad. Skin around the stitches is red and warm. I do not see the wound opening up.

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you. On examination the right groin scar is about six centimetres. It is red around, tender to press, and there is a small bead of yellow discharge at the lower end. The edges are together.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): There is no fluctuance and no red streak running up the abdomen.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah, it pains when you press there.

[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry. Thinking aloud, this could be a superficial wound infection, or only a stitch reaction with a little fluid. I am not calling it either one yet. Let us see what the tests say.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): To be plain, both remain possible and I cannot rule out either. That is only a working impression, not a confirmed diagnosis.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I need another operation? I am quite scared.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): I cannot see a collection to drain today, so no further operation from this visit.
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): I want a wound swab for culture, and a full blood count, both today.
[SEG0054] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can swab once you finish, and send him downstairs for the blood test.
[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please do the swab today and the blood count today. No scan unless things worsen.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): The old antibiotic is finished. Will you change it?
[SEG0057] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. I am starting flucloxacillin five hundred milligram, by mouth, four times a day, for seven days, for this wound. Start today.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): Four times, for seven days. Should I keep the Crocin?
[SEG0059] person_3 (DOCTOR): Continue paracetamol five hundred milligrams, up to four times a day if you need it for pain or fever. Do not restart the ibuprofen.
[SEG0060] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep the wound dry. No oil, no powder, no home paste. Change the gauze if it is wet, with clean hands.
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): The bank wants me back. I don't know if sitting all day is okay. The traffic itself is tiring.
[SEG0062] person_3 (DOCTOR): Light desk work is alright if you feel up to it. No lifting and no gym for a few more weeks. That is advice only.
[SEG0063] person_2 (PATIENT): And last night's temperature, was it too much?

[SEG0064] person_3 (DOCTOR): A hundred and one point two at home, thirty seven point eight here, pulse ninety six, pressure one thirty over eighty four. Not an emergency number, but with discharge we do not ignore it.
[SEG0065] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will see you again in two days for a wound check. The desk can book it.
[SEG0066] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I will book the surgical clinic in two days.
[SEG0067] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the redness spreads, or the fever comes back, or you feel very unwell, come the same day, do not wait.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): If it spreads I will come the same day. I don't know, doctor, did the oil cause this?
[SEG0069] person_3 (DOCTOR): I cannot say the oil caused it. Just stop using it. We will go by the swab result, not by guessing.
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay doctor. I will collect the new tablet and start today. Thank you.
[SEG0071] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I will take the swab now. Kindly hold still, then I will walk you for the blood test.

spec.situation: Patient 10 days after a hernia, appendix or caesarean operation; wound redness and discharge, fever the night before; nurse removes dressing and describes it; patient is vague about antibiotic course ('five days... or was it seven'); wound swab and antibiotic change.
features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Augmentin, maybe 625 mg, TID, finished; duration and dose uncertain, not approximately confirmed.
bad.text: Augmentin (generic_name=amoxicillin-clavulanate, dose=625 mg, frequency=three times a day, duration=approximately 5 to 7 days, status=discontinued, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: The patient had been applying coconut oil to the wound and stopped yesterday; doctor specifically advised not to use oil, turmeric, or any paste.
Augmentin course length was uncertain because the patient said it was 'five days... or was it seven?' and had finished the strip.
Ibuprofen 400 mg twice a day was stopped two days ago because of acidity.
Paracetamol was being taken when needed for pain ('when it pains'), not simply scheduled twice daily; doctor advised it could be continued up to four times a day as needed for pain or fever.
Lactulose had been prescribed after surgery but the patient never took it even once.
The patient denied any drug allergy specifically including penicillin, not just allergies generally.
Wound pain was reported as worse than last week.
The patient was specifically asked whether pain worsened on walking and whether the discharge was foul smelling; he was unsure about both, and the doctor stated these were not definite features.
The doctor documented no scan unless things worsen.
The doctor said there was no further operation needed from this visit because no collection was seen to drain today.
